question: Should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout after the branch is refreshed?
rationale: The code shape is focused and privacy-protective, but disabling existing opt-ins and adding a Play Data Safety upload lane are upgrade and release-policy choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Accept reset and rollout
options.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh the branch, and land the PR.

options.title: Revise disclosure first
options.body: Request wording, placement, consent-version, or release-lane changes if Play review or product policy needs a different disclosure shape.

options.title: Hold for release materials
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged until the Data Safety CSV, Play Console state, privacy policy, and review artifacts are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Accept reset and rollout
recommendation.body: Approve the legacy opt-in reset, verify Play Console/Data Safety/privacy materials, refresh the branch, and land the PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Android release ownership and the current-main Android conflict surface make steipete the best available owner for the release/compatibility decision.
